segments.he: צְרִיכִין לִבְטחַ בַּה' וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה לא תִּמְנָעֵהוּ הַפַּרְנָסָה
segments.en: And this is also the aspect of the taking of Esther into the house of Achashverosh, when she cried: "My G-d, my G-d, why have You forsaken me?" [Tehillim 22:2] — as our Sages, of blessed memory, said [Megillah 15a]. And through this came the fall of Haman the Amalekite — who represents the power of the impurity of the sitra achra — all in the above manner, to show Israel that even in contaminated places they should cry out to G-d and seek and find Him. As Mordechai and Esther then did — they gathered all the Jews to cry out greatly to G-d. And so in every generation — collectively all of Israel, and individually each and every person — one must always seek G-d in every place, and cry out at all times to G-d in the manner of "From the belly of the grave I cried out". And one must never despair of crying and seeking, ever — until G-d looks down and sees from heaven.

segments.he: וּבְוַדַּאי הִיא עֵצָה גְּדוֹלָה וְקַלָּה שֶׁהַכּל יְכוֹלִין לְקַיְּמָהּ. כִּי יְכוֹלִין לִזְכּוֹת לִתְשׁוּבָה וּלְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר לְבַד.
segments.en: A person must remove from his mind each day and every time everything that has passed upon him up to that day and that hour — and it should not enter his reckoning at all, as if he has never yet begun at all. For if you will contemplate and understand the matter of the descents and falls that befall each person — the essential fall of each person's mind is because it seems to him that he has already tested himself and begun somewhat in the service of G-d, and fell from this — and afterward strengthened himself to begin again and fell again — and so it was many times. Therefore the evil inclination entices him to despair of himself completely, saying in his heart: "See, there is no hope" — as all who engage in the holy learning of drawing the youth close to the service of G-d know.

segments.he: אַךְ יֵשׁ עַל זֶה מְנִיעָה גְּדוֹלָה וַעֲצוּמָה וְהִיא מְנִיעַת הַפַּרְנָסָה שֶׁכָּל אָדָם טָרוּד בְּפַרְנָסָתוֹ מְאד וְעַל כֵּן אֵינוֹ עוֹסֵק בִּשְׁלֵמוּת אֲפִלּוּ בְּעֵצָה קַלָּה הַזּאת לָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁל הָעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁבָּאַלְפָא בֵּיתָא. אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם זֶה אֵינוֹ מְנִיעָה כְּלָל. כִּי צְרִיכִין לְהַזְכִּיר אֶת עַצְמוֹ הָאֱמֶת שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּשׁוּם אפֶן לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לְעַצְמוֹ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעָתוֹ וְטִרְחָתוֹ. כִּי זֶהוּ כְּפִירָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לוֹמַר כּחִי וְעצֶם יָדִי עָשָׂה לִי וְכוּ' חַס וְשָׁלוֹם רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלָן. רַק צְרִיכִין לְהַאֲמִין בַּה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי כָּל הַפַּרְנָסָה הִוא מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דְּבָרִים ח') וְזָכַרְתָּ אֶת ה' אֱלקֶיךָ כִּי הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן לְךָ כּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חַיִל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִזְמוֹר זֶה עֵינֵי כל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ וְאַתָּה נוֹתֵן לָהֶם אֶת אָכְלָם בְּעִתּוֹ פּוֹתֵחַ וְכוּ' וּמַשְׂבִּיעַ וְכוּ'. וְזֶהוּ מַעֲלַת זֶה הַמִּזְמוֹר דְּאִית בֵּהּ תַּרְתֵּי יַחַד שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּא"ב וְנִזְכָּר בּוֹ פַּרְנָסָה שֶׁהִיא מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה מֻבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא. כִּי מִי שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה בְּוַדַּאי יִזְכֶּה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא. כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְהַהִתְקָרְבוּת אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא.
segments.en: But whoever merits to attach himself to upright and true companions always, until he merits to receive and establish in his heart the above holy counsel to forget each time everything that has passed upon him — even if he has already begun thousands and tens of thousands of times without number — now he should begin anew, to prepare and ready himself with whatever he can, whether to cry to G-d from the depth of the heart as is needed in that very hour, or to begin to study and pray and engage in mitzvos, or to gladden his soul with what "He has not made me a gentile," "and He has separated us from those who err," and to transform sadness and sighing to joy — through all this, he will remain standing in the fulfillment of the Torah always.

segments.he: דְּהַיְנוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לְהִתְיַגֵּעַ וְלִטְרחַ בַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ הַצַּדִּיקִים וְהַכְּשֵׁרִים וְהַחֲסִידִים שֶׁלְּפָנֵינוּ שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ הַקְּטַנִּים שֶׁבָּהֶם יָגְעוּ וְטָרְחוּ מְאד מְאד בְּתַעֲנִיתִים רַבִּים וּבְסִגּוּפִים קָשִׁים וַעֲצוּמִים רַבִּים מְאד. וְאִם אֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לָזֶה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁהָיָה צָרִיךְ לָזֶה לְפִי עֲוֹנוֹתָיו וּפְגָמָיו הַמְרֻבִּים. וַאֲפִלּוּ אִם יוֹדֵעַ בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁגַּם עַתָּה עוֹבֵר עָלָיו מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר בְּכָל עֵת וְכוּ'. אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אִם לא יַנִּיחַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ לִפּל לְעוֹלָם וִיחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְדַבֵּר דִּבּוּרִים עַל כָּל פָּנִים תָּמִיד לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּצְעָקוֹת וּתְחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת הַרְבֵּה לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּוַדַּאי סוֹף כָּל סוֹף יָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכַנַּ"ל. אַךְ שֶׁלּא יִמְנָעֵהוּ מִזֶּה הַפַּרְנָסָה רַק יִבְטַח בַּה' שֶׁהוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ יְפַרְנְסוֹ בְּרַחֲמָיו כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִזְמוֹר זֶה כַּנַּ"ל.
segments.en: All the confusions of evil thoughts are the aspect of the crookedness and depth of the sitra achra, G-d spare us. Therefore the essential counsel is simplicity and sincerity — to train oneself not to walk with cleverness, and not to think any superfluous thoughts. Rather, to strip one's thought to the ultimate simplicity and sincerity, and not to multiply thinking about anything — especially regarding that evil desire, of which there are people who have terrible investigations and thoughts and evil reflections regarding this repulsiveness. For a spirit of actual folly and madness has become attached to their thoughts, until they think what they think — as they themselves know, G-d spare us. And through this they arrive at what they arrive at, G-d spare us. And to be saved from this — it is only through the paths of the sincerity and simplicity of the true Tzaddik. For multiplying thoughts — even as a refutation, to nullify this desire — also causes the desire to grow stronger, as it is written in the Sefer HaAleph-Beis: "Do not enter with your enticements into argument and counter-argument." And it is impossible to explain all this in writing. But the essential counsel is the aspect of great simplicity and sincerity, and to cry out greatly to G-d. For certainly whoever has already been ensnared in this — each one according to his level — must not despair of himself at all. Rather, to cry out each time to G-d from whatever place he is, and to grab hold of his thought at each time to turn it from the depth of the sitra achra to the straight path — to the aspect of the sincerity and simplicity of the true Tzaddik.

segments.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ אִם הוּא בַּעַל מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן אוֹ מְלָאכָה, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יֵדַע הָאֱמֶת כִּי לא בְּכחַ יִגְבַּר אִישׁ. וְאִם יַעֲשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל פַּרְנָסָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעָתוֹ וְטִרְחָתוֹ לְבַד כִּי אִם בִּישׁוּעַת ה' וְחַסְדּוֹ. כַּאֲשֶׁר יוֹדֵעַ כָּל אֶחָד בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁעִקַּר הַפַּרְנָסָה כְּשֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ אֵיזֶה רֶוַח וְכַיּוֹצֵא. וּמִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן הַטְּרָדוֹת וְהַדְּאָגוֹת שֶׁאֵינָם מוֹעִילִים כְּלָל אַדְּרַבָּא מַזִּיקִים הַרְבֵּה לַפַּרְנָסָה. עַל כֵּן אֲפִלּוּ הַבַּעַל מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן וּמְלָאכָה יָכוֹל לִמְצא לְנַפְשׁוֹ כַּמָּה שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם שֶׁיַּעֲסֹק בָּהֶם בַּאֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים וְהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְכוּ' לְקַדֵּשׁ הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל הָא"ב וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָשׁוּב בְּוַדַּאי לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ. נִמְצָא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָאֵלּוּ תַּרְתֵּי שֶׁכָּלוּל הַמִּזְמוֹר מֵהֶם שֶׁהֵם הָא"ב שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל הַדִּבּוּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהַזְכָּרַת שֶׁבַח פַּרְנָסָה שֶׁהוּא מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּוַדַּאי נָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְעַל כֵּן זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי מִזְמוֹר זֶה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא. מֵאַחַר שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ שָׁבִין לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכַנַּ"ל.
segments.en: And this is the essential teshuvah — the aspect of "Return, O backsliding children of Israel" [Yeshayahu 31:6], and it is written "the apostates have gone deeply into perversity" [Hoshea 5:2], and: "They have deeply corrupted themselves" [ibid. 9:9], and: "I have come into deep waters" [Tehillim 69:3]. And one who does not return in teshuvah, Heaven forfend, about him it is written: "those who pass through the valley of weeping" [ibid. 84:7]. Therefore one must strive to rescue one's soul from the pit, and to flee to the true Tzaddikim and to the sincere and upright who are attached to them — so that one can strengthen oneself to emerge and flee from the depth of the sitra achra, to draw oneself to the paths of sincerity and simplicity — through which one merits to purify one's thought, which is the essential holiness of Rosh Hashanah. And this is all our crying out on Rosh Hashanah — to merit to purify the thought. And this is why we cry on Rosh Hashanah: "Out of the depths I call to You, Hashem" [Tehillim 130:1] — depths precisely. For from all kinds of depths one must only cry and call to G-d — to merit to the paths of simplicity and sincerity through which is the essential purity of thought. For there are ten depths — the depth of good and the depth of evil, and so on [as cited in Sefer Yetzirah] — and even from the depth of good one must cry to G-d. For even good thoughts — one must not delve into them too much, beyond the limit — lest one go outside the boundary, Heaven forfend. And even one who merits to good thoughts and to delving into them properly — even so, one must each time call to G-d from them, that G-d take him from them and raise him to a higher level. And this is impossible except through simplicity and sincerity — by which one strips one's mind at all times as if one knows nothing at all — and through this one merits each time to a higher level, by crying each time to G-d in simplicity and sincerity as if one has never known anything. As is understood and explained from all the holy conversations of our Master, Teacher, and Rebbe, of blessed memory. And all the more and more so whoever is not at the summit of perfection in knowledge — and how much more so one who is dominated by the evil depth — how much must he cry from the depths: "Out of the depths I call to You, Hashem" — to merit to nullify the evil depth of the sitra achra into which he has fallen. And this is the aspect of "From the belly of the grave I cried out" [Yonah 2:3], mentioned at the end of the above Torah.

In truth and in absolute truth, there is nothing that stands in the way of teshuvah. And even though it is written "All those who come to her do not return" [Mishlei 2:19], and it is stated in the Zohar that teshuvah does not help for the blemish of drops of the brain [i.e., the sin of wasting seed] — even so, in truth teshuvah does help, as is cited in all the books of ethics. And as I heard explicitly from the mouth of our Rebbe, of blessed memory — only because one has blemished so greatly, one must be tested and refined and withstand this trial of distance. That is, to be distanced so greatly in all kinds of distancing — that it is written about him that teshuvah does not help. And when one is a fool and simpleton and does not take pity on oneself not to lose one's world — then one finds an excuse to distance oneself from teshuvah, since it is already written that teshuvah does not help. But whoever truly thinks about his purpose and has compassion upon himself — then even though he sees all kinds of distancing in the world, and even if it is written about him that teshuvah will not help — even so he does not look at this at all. On the contrary — he has even more compassion for himself: what will ultimately become of him, and what will he do on the day of reckoning? And whoever does not wish to deceive himself and not to lose his world — everything he finds and sees that distances him more, he has even more compassion for himself, and cries out to G-d more and more from the depth of his heart — until G-d looks down and sees from heaven. For truly G-d desires kindness, and there is nothing that stands in the way of teshuvah. And we have found already many great wicked people who blemished drops of the brain and denied fundamental principles — and yet were accepted in teshuvah. And then when one merits to withstand this trial and return in complete teshuvah even while it seems one is being distanced — then G-d has compassion on him and he draws close precisely through this — through having withstood this trial of distancing. Understand well.

aligned_segments.he: צְרִיכִין לִבְטחַ בַּה' וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה לא תִּמְנָעֵהוּ הַפַּרְנָסָה
aligned_segments.en: And this is also the aspect of the taking of Esther into the house of Achashverosh, when she cried: "My G-d, my G-d, why have You forsaken me?" [Tehillim 22:2] — as our Sages, of blessed memory, said [Megillah 15a]. And through this came the fall of Haman the Amalekite — who represents the power of the impurity of the sitra achra — all in the above manner, to show Israel that even in contaminated places they should cry out to G-d and seek and find Him. As Mordechai and Esther then did — they gathered all the Jews to cry out greatly to G-d. And so in every generation — collectively all of Israel, and individually each and every person — one must always seek G-d in every place, and cry out at all times to G-d in the manner of "From the belly of the grave I cried out". And one must never despair of crying and seeking, ever — until G-d looks down and sees from heaven.

aligned_segments.he: וּבְוַדַּאי הִיא עֵצָה גְּדוֹלָה וְקַלָּה שֶׁהַכּל יְכוֹלִין לְקַיְּמָהּ.
aligned_segments.en: A person must remove from his mind each day and every time everything that has passed upon him up to that day and that hour — and it should not enter his reckoning at all, as if he has never yet begun at all.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי יְכוֹלִין לִזְכּוֹת לִתְשׁוּבָה וּלְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר לְבַד.
aligned_segments.en: For if you will contemplate and understand the matter of the descents and falls that befall each person — the essential fall of each person's mind is because it seems to him that he has already tested himself and begun somewhat in the service of G-d, and fell from this — and afterward strengthened himself to begin again and fell again — and so it was many times. Therefore the evil inclination entices him to despair of himself completely, saying in his heart: "See, there is no hope" — as all who engage in the holy learning of drawing the youth close to the service of G-d know.

aligned_segments.he: אַךְ יֵשׁ עַל זֶה מְנִיעָה גְּדוֹלָה וַעֲצוּמָה וְהִיא מְנִיעַת הַפַּרְנָסָה שֶׁכָּל אָדָם טָרוּד בְּפַרְנָסָתוֹ מְאד וְעַל כֵּן אֵינוֹ עוֹסֵק בִּשְׁלֵמוּת אֲפִלּוּ בְּעֵצָה קַלָּה הַזּאת לָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁל הָעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁבָּאַלְפָא בֵּיתָא. אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם זֶה אֵינוֹ מְנִיעָה כְּלָל. כִּי צְרִיכִין לְהַזְכִּיר אֶת עַצְמוֹ הָאֱמֶת שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּשׁוּם אפֶן לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לְעַצְמוֹ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעָתוֹ וְטִרְחָתוֹ. כִּי זֶהוּ כְּפִירָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לוֹמַר כּחִי וְעצֶם יָדִי עָשָׂה לִי וְכוּ' חַס וְשָׁלוֹם רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלָן. רַק צְרִיכִין לְהַאֲמִין בַּה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי כָּל הַפַּרְנָסָה הִוא מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דְּבָרִים ח') וְזָכַרְתָּ אֶת ה' אֱלקֶיךָ כִּי הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן לְךָ כּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת חַיִל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִזְמוֹר זֶה עֵינֵי כל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ וְאַתָּה נוֹתֵן לָהֶם אֶת אָכְלָם בְּעִתּוֹ פּוֹתֵחַ וְכוּ' וּמַשְׂבִּיעַ וְכוּ'. וְזֶהוּ מַעֲלַת זֶה הַמִּזְמוֹר דְּאִית בֵּהּ תַּרְתֵּי יַחַד שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּא"ב וְנִזְכָּר בּוֹ פַּרְנָסָה שֶׁהִיא מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְעַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי זֶה מֻבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא. כִּי מִי שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה בְּוַדַּאי יִזְכֶּה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא. כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה וְהַהִתְקָרְבוּת אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא.
aligned_segments.en: But whoever merits to attach himself to upright and true companions always, until he merits to receive and establish in his heart the above holy counsel to forget each time everything that has passed upon him — even if he has already begun thousands and tens of thousands of times without number — now he should begin anew, to prepare and ready himself with whatever he can, whether to cry to G-d from the depth of the heart as is needed in that very hour, or to begin to study and pray and engage in mitzvos, or to gladden his soul with what "He has not made me a gentile," "and He has separated us from those who err," and to transform sadness and sighing to joy — through all this, he will remain standing in the fulfillment of the Torah always.

aligned_segments.he: דְּהַיְנוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לְהִתְיַגֵּעַ וְלִטְרחַ בַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ הַצַּדִּיקִים וְהַכְּשֵׁרִים וְהַחֲסִידִים שֶׁלְּפָנֵינוּ שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ הַקְּטַנִּים שֶׁבָּהֶם יָגְעוּ וְטָרְחוּ מְאד מְאד בְּתַעֲנִיתִים רַבִּים וּבְסִגּוּפִים קָשִׁים וַעֲצוּמִים רַבִּים מְאד.
aligned_segments.en: All the confusions of evil thoughts are the aspect of the crookedness and depth of the sitra achra, G-d spare us. Therefore the essential counsel is simplicity and sincerity — to train oneself not to walk with cleverness, and not to think any superfluous thoughts.

aligned_segments.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לָזֶה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁהָיָה צָרִיךְ לָזֶה לְפִי עֲוֹנוֹתָיו וּפְגָמָיו הַמְרֻבִּים.
aligned_segments.en: Rather, to strip one's thought to the ultimate simplicity and sincerity, and not to multiply thinking about anything — especially regarding that evil desire, of which there are people who have terrible investigations and thoughts and evil reflections regarding this repulsiveness. For a spirit of actual folly and madness has become attached to their thoughts, until they think what they think — as they themselves know, G-d spare us.

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ אִם יוֹדֵעַ בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁגַּם עַתָּה עוֹבֵר עָלָיו מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר בְּכָל עֵת וְכוּ'.
aligned_segments.en: And through this they arrive at what they arrive at, G-d spare us. And to be saved from this — it is only through the paths of the sincerity and simplicity of the true Tzaddik.

aligned_segments.he: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אִם לא יַנִּיחַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ לִפּל לְעוֹלָם וִיחַזֵּק אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְדַבֵּר דִּבּוּרִים עַל כָּל פָּנִים תָּמִיד לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּצְעָקוֹת וּתְחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת הַרְבֵּה לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּוַדַּאי סוֹף כָּל סוֹף יָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכַנַּ"ל.
aligned_segments.en: For multiplying thoughts — even as a refutation, to nullify this desire — also causes the desire to grow stronger, as it is written in the Sefer HaAleph-Beis: "Do not enter with your enticements into argument and counter-argument." And it is impossible to explain all this in writing. But the essential counsel is the aspect of great simplicity and sincerity, and to cry out greatly to G-d.

aligned_segments.he: אַךְ שֶׁלּא יִמְנָעֵהוּ מִזֶּה הַפַּרְנָסָה רַק יִבְטַח בַּה' שֶׁהוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ יְפַרְנְסוֹ בְּרַחֲמָיו כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִזְמוֹר זֶה כַּנַּ"ל.
aligned_segments.en: For certainly whoever has already been ensnared in this — each one according to his level — must not despair of himself at all. Rather, to cry out each time to G-d from whatever place he is, and to grab hold of his thought at each time to turn it from the depth of the sitra achra to the straight path — to the aspect of the sincerity and simplicity of the true Tzaddik.

aligned_segments.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ אִם הוּא בַּעַל מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן אוֹ מְלָאכָה, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יֵדַע הָאֱמֶת כִּי לא בְּכחַ יִגְבַּר אִישׁ.
aligned_segments.en: And this is the essential teshuvah — the aspect of "Return, O backsliding children of Israel" [Yeshayahu 31:6], and it is written "the apostates have gone deeply into perversity" [Hoshea 5:2], and: "They have deeply corrupted themselves" [ibid. 9:9], and: "I have come into deep waters" [Tehillim 69:3].

aligned_segments.he: וְאִם יַעֲשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל פַּרְנָסָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעָתוֹ וְטִרְחָתוֹ לְבַד כִּי אִם בִּישׁוּעַת ה' וְחַסְדּוֹ.
aligned_segments.en: And one who does not return in teshuvah, Heaven forfend, about him it is written: "those who pass through the valley of weeping" [ibid. 84:7]. Therefore one must strive to rescue one's soul from the pit, and to flee to the true Tzaddikim and to the sincere and upright who are attached to them — so that one can strengthen oneself to emerge and flee from the depth of the sitra achra, to draw oneself to the paths of sincerity and simplicity — through which one merits to purify one's thought, which is the essential holiness of Rosh Hashanah.

aligned_segments.he: כַּאֲשֶׁר יוֹדֵעַ כָּל אֶחָד בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁעִקַּר הַפַּרְנָסָה כְּשֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ אֵיזֶה רֶוַח וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
aligned_segments.en: And this is all our crying out on Rosh Hashanah — to merit to purify the thought.

aligned_segments.he: וּמִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן הַטְּרָדוֹת וְהַדְּאָגוֹת שֶׁאֵינָם מוֹעִילִים כְּלָל אַדְּרַבָּא מַזִּיקִים הַרְבֵּה לַפַּרְנָסָה.
aligned_segments.en: And this is why we cry on Rosh Hashanah: "Out of the depths I call to You, Hashem" [Tehillim 130:1] — depths precisely. For from all kinds of depths one must only cry and call to G-d — to merit to the paths of simplicity and sincerity through which is the essential purity of thought.

aligned_segments.he: עַל כֵּן אֲפִלּוּ הַבַּעַל מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן וּמְלָאכָה יָכוֹל לִמְצא לְנַפְשׁוֹ כַּמָּה שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם שֶׁיַּעֲסֹק בָּהֶם בַּאֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים וְהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְכוּ' לְקַדֵּשׁ הַדִּבּוּר שֶׁל הָא"ב וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָשׁוּב בְּוַדַּאי לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ.
aligned_segments.en: For there are ten depths — the depth of good and the depth of evil, and so on [as cited in Sefer Yetzirah] — and even from the depth of good one must cry to G-d. For even good thoughts — one must not delve into them too much, beyond the limit — lest one go outside the boundary, Heaven forfend.

aligned_segments.he: נִמְצָא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָאֵלּוּ תַּרְתֵּי שֶׁכָּלוּל הַמִּזְמוֹר מֵהֶם שֶׁהֵם הָא"ב שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל הַדִּבּוּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהַזְכָּרַת שֶׁבַח פַּרְנָסָה שֶׁהוּא מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּוַדַּאי נָשׁוּב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ.
aligned_segments.en: And even one who merits to good thoughts and to delving into them properly — even so, one must each time call to G-d from them, that G-d take him from them and raise him to a higher level.

aligned_segments.he: וְעַל כֵּן זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי מִזְמוֹר זֶה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
aligned_segments.en: And this is impossible except through simplicity and sincerity — by which one strips one's mind at all times as if one knows nothing at all — and through this one merits each time to a higher level, by crying each time to G-d in simplicity and sincerity as if one has never known anything. As is understood and explained from all the holy conversations of our Master, Teacher, and Rebbe, of blessed memory.

aligned_segments.he: מֵאַחַר שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ שָׁבִין לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכַנַּ"ל.
aligned_segments.en: And all the more and more so whoever is not at the summit of perfection in knowledge — and how much more so one who is dominated by the evil depth — how much must he cry from the depths: "Out of the depths I call to You, Hashem" — to merit to nullify the evil depth of the sitra achra into which he has fallen. And this is the aspect of "From the belly of the grave I cried out" [Yonah 2:3], mentioned at the end of the above Torah.

In truth and in absolute truth, there is nothing that stands in the way of teshuvah. And even though it is written "All those who come to her do not return" [Mishlei 2:19], and it is stated in the Zohar that teshuvah does not help for the blemish of drops of the brain [i.e., the sin of wasting seed] — even so, in truth teshuvah does help, as is cited in all the books of ethics. And as I heard explicitly from the mouth of our Rebbe, of blessed memory — only because one has blemished so greatly, one must be tested and refined and withstand this trial of distance. That is, to be distanced so greatly in all kinds of distancing — that it is written about him that teshuvah does not help. And when one is a fool and simpleton and does not take pity on oneself not to lose one's world — then one finds an excuse to distance oneself from teshuvah, since it is already written that teshuvah does not help. But whoever truly thinks about his purpose and has compassion upon himself — then even though he sees all kinds of distancing in the world, and even if it is written about him that teshuvah will not help — even so he does not look at this at all. On the contrary — he has even more compassion for himself: what will ultimately become of him, and what will he do on the day of reckoning? And whoever does not wish to deceive himself and not to lose his world — everything he finds and sees that distances him more, he has even more compassion for himself, and cries out to G-d more and more from the depth of his heart — until G-d looks down and sees from heaven. For truly G-d desires kindness, and there is nothing that stands in the way of teshuvah. And we have found already many great wicked people who blemished drops of the brain and denied fundamental principles — and yet were accepted in teshuvah. And then when one merits to withstand this trial and return in complete teshuvah even while it seems one is being distanced — then G-d has compassion on him and he draws close precisely through this — through having withstood this trial of distancing. Understand well.
